sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aarushi Khare
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant; learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.131 of 2023, under Sections 376(3), 366, 363 I.P.C. and Section 5(L)/6 of the POCSO Act, P.S. Govind Nagar, District Kanpur Nagar, during pendency of the trial.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive; as per ossification test, victim is more than 17 years.

Counsel for the applicant next submits that from the statement of victim recorded under Shailesh Sahu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62427665/
1 Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., it is evident that victim on her own sweet will, went with the applicant and they solemnized marriage and the marriage has been registered by the marriage officer; the statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. and medical report of the victim are not supporting the prosecution case.

entities.text: Shailesh Sahu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, there is no prospect of trial of the present case being concluded in near future.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 16.06.2023 and in case, he is enlarged on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

5. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh Vs. State of U.P. and another reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Dataram Singh Vs. State of U.P. and another reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Let the applicant, Shailesh Sahu who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
7.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
